items.title: Why did Apple buy AI music startup Samplab, and how might this impact Logic Pro?
items.excerpt: Apple acquired AI audio startup Samplab (disclosed via an EU Digital Markets Act filing), seemingly to bolster Logic Pro's AI tools such as polyphonic audio-to-MIDI and note editing.

items.title: Stop sending me vibecoded AI plugins, I'm begging you
items.excerpt: MusicTech's inbox is drowning in vibecoded plugins; the piece explains why that is a problem for producers and which indie developers are using AI coding responsibly.

history_match.title: Who's Buying All These Vibe-Coded Plugins?

items.title: Deezer Announces 'On/Off Toggle' for AI Audio, Enabling Users to Remove Fully AI-Generated Music
items.excerpt: Deezer announced an AI audio on/off toggle that will let users remove fully AI-generated music from their experience, building on its AI detection and tagging system.

history_match.title: Deezer to let users block AI-generated music from search results

items.title: YouTube Music Adds Labels for Tracks 'Created Primarily' With Gen AI
items.excerpt: YouTube Music began labelling songs 'created primarily using generative AI' on 14 October, using its own detection system, saying listeners asked for transparency.

history_match.title: YouTube Music launches new labels as AI-generated music floods streaming platforms

items.title: Sony Music, UMG File New Legal Action Against DistroKid to Force Disclosure of AI Uploads
items.excerpt: Universal Music Group and Sony Music filed a legal action to force DistroKid to disclose how many AI-generated songs (including Suno output) it delivers to DSPs.

history_match.title: UMG & Sony Demand DistroKid Tell How Many AI Songs It Uploads From Suno: 'Staggering Scale'

items.title: Major labels are getting 'massive corporate payouts' for AI licensing but 'paying musicians zero', says AFM's 'Human Made Human Paid' campaign
items.excerpt: US performer union AFM launched a campaign demanding musician consent and pay before recordings are used in label AI licensing deals.

history_match.title: 'Human Made, Human Paid': The Largest U.S. Musicians Union Is Demanding AI Protections

items.title: Elektron Responds To Explosion Of Unofficial Firmware
items.excerpt: EZBOT shares takeaways from an hour-long call with Elektron about AI and its impact on the company, and the wave of AI-assisted hacked firmware for its devices.

items.title: Romain Gavras Is Bummed About Those AI Versions of 'Storm'
items.excerpt: Director Romain Gavras says AI copycat 'recreations' of his Yung Lean 'Storm' video made him sad for the crew who put in so much work on the real thing.

items.title: Streaming Fraud Threatens More Than Fraudsters. We Must Find Meaningful Solutions (Guest Column)
items.excerpt: NMPA chief David Israelite argues streaming fraud, exacerbated by AI-generated tracks (Deezer: 90,000 a day), drains songwriter royalties and needs industry solutions.

history_match.title: U.S. Copyright Office Opens Music Streaming Fraud Inquiry, Probing Prevalence & 'Potential Solutions'

items.title: IAMDDB accuses Israel of 'stealing her identity' in AI propaganda video
items.excerpt: Manchester artist IAMDDB says a now-deleted government clip used an AI-generated likeness of her, raising artist-likeness and deepfake concerns.

items.title: Apple's latest acquisition suggests Logic Pro is getting Melodyne-style polyphonic note editing
items.excerpt: AI audio company Samplab was acquired by Apple in June per EU disclosures, hinting at Melodyne-style polyphonic editing coming to Logic Pro. (Same story as MusicTech item.)

items.title: Moises and SoundCloud Partner to Bring AI-Supported Creation, Collaboration and Distribution Together for 150+ Million Artists
items.excerpt: Moises, the ethically trained AI creative suite used by 80 million musicians, is partnering with SoundCloud to bring stem separation, chord/lyric detection and AI-assisted mixing and mastering together with SoundCloud distribution. SoundCloud says it does not train generative models on artists' music without consent.

items.title: As fans reject AI-generated music, even boosters are drawing the line
items.excerpt: Guardian analysis: streaming services, musicians and fans are drawing lines on AI-generated music, and even enthusiasts like Grimes and A$AP Rocky say they embrace AI content but won't produce it themselves. (Background mentions Spotify's 50m-track slop removal, which was already covered; this piece takes the wider artist-sentiment angle.)

items.title: AI 음악 기술 '뉴튠', 오디오비주얼 에이전트 DJ '탈' ADE 2026서 첫 공개
items.excerpt: Korean AI music company Neutune is premiering 'Tal', an audiovisual agent DJ built on traditional Korean mask motifs, at Amsterdam Dance Event 2026. The project was made with KOCCA's 2026 AI content production grant.

items.title: Korea's JYP Partners and SM pursue AI idols to personalize fan service
items.excerpt: K-pop agencies JYP (via JYP Partners) and SM are pursuing AI idols and backing startups to test personalized AI idol fan services and build new IP.

items.title: Elephant In the Room Reminder: Major Hits from Kylie Minogue and Nick Cave Already Used to Train AI Without Compensation, the ICMP Tells Australian Legislators
items.excerpt: Global publishers' body ICMP told Australian legislators that AI models have already been trained on songs by Kylie Minogue and Nick Cave without permission or payment, and warned that a text-and-data-mining carve-out would 'legitimize larceny'.

items.title: Is There a Future for 'Humanoid Robot Performances'? South Korea's Galaxy Corporation Thinks So
items.excerpt: Galaxy Corporation, a Korean 'physical AI' entertainment-tech company combining K-pop IP, AI and humanoid robots, is staging a Halloween robot-performance event in Saratoga, California on October 30. Weak AI angle: the AI is about robotics more than the music itself.

items.title: Chronixx calls for separate Grammy category for AI albums
items.excerpt: Ahead of the 2027 Grammy race, reggae singer Chronixx has called for albums made with large language models and machine learning to compete in their own Grammy category. In reggae and dancehall, the AI debate already covers songwriting, visuals, voice imitation and training data.

items.title: Lithuanian lawmakers propose legal protection against AI voice cloning
items.excerpt: Lithuanian MPs proposed Civil Code amendments creating a legal right to one's voice, so reproducing, publishing or otherwise using it, including AI-generated imitations, would need consent. Music angle is indirect: this is a general voice-likeness law.
